# Commissioning spec and point-mapping fixtures

What the commissioning readers are tested against (design note `docs/design/commissioning.md`,
"Test-spec file" and "Point mapping"; issue #658). `tests/commissioning/` reads them.

| Path | What it is | Regenerated by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listing_12_1.json` | OBC §12.7 **Listing 12.1**, "Configuration of test setup", verbatim. | nobody: it is the published text |
| `listing_12_2.json` | OBC §12.7 **Listing 12.2**, "Example `pointNameMapping` file", verbatim. | nobody: it is the published text |
| `listing_12_1_commented.json` | **Not a published listing.** Listing 12.1 with `//` and `/* */` comments added, written for this repository's tests: comments before and after the document, at line ends, between a key and its value, over several lines, holding quotes, braces, a stray `*/`, a `/*` and a character outside ASCII, and a last line with no line feed. Every value is the listing's, so it loads to the same spec. | nobody: edit it by hand |
| `building_33.json` | The JSON block of the design note's "Worked spec: Building 33 cooling-coil valve (§12.6)", copied by hand. No test reads the note (a test that did would put it on the classifier's test-read list), so when that block changes, copy it again. | copy the block again when the note changes |
| `every_field.json` | A hand-written spec that uses every key of the format in an awkward spelling: members out of order, a tab, comments, `\u` escapes in keys and strings, raw characters outside ASCII and an astral one, comment markers inside a string, numbers at the canonical form's thresholds (`1e-4`, `0.00001`, `1e16`), `-0` and `-0.0`, an inline mapping, a `csv` and a `combiTimeTable` source, every list present and empty, override keys that are not in sorted order, and Scenario 1 fields holding `null`, nested lists and an integer past 2^53. | nobody: edit it by hand |
| `canonical/<name>.json` | The canonical form of each file above. `canonical/listing_12_1_commented.json` is byte-identical to `canonical/listing_12_1.json`, which a test requires. | `derive_canonical.py`, by hand |
| `derive_canonical.py` | The independent derivation of the canonical goldens and their ids. | nobody: it is the reference |

| `trends/trends_oracle.txt` | The digests, the merged cells and what replay feeds the engine at each frame, derived independently. | `python3 -I derive_trends.py trends_oracle.txt` in `trends/`, by hand; never blessed |

## Where the two listings come from

- **Source:** the OpenBuildingControl specification, chapter 12 "Verification", §12.7
  "Specification for Automating the Verification", §12.7.2 "Scenario 1: Control Input Obtained by
  Simulating a CDL Model": <https://obc.lbl.gov/specification/verification.html>.
- **Read on:** 2026-11-21.
- **How:** the page was fetched with `curl`, and the text of the two listings' `<pre>` blocks was
  taken as it is: the syntax-highlighting `<span>` tags removed and the HTML entities unescaped
  (`&quot;` to `"`), nothing else changed. Each file ends with the one line feed its block ends
  with. Listing 12.1 is 1,079 bytes and Listing 12.2 is 1,953 bytes; `tests/commissioning/listings.rs`
  pins both lengths and an FNV-1a-128 hash of each, so an edit to either fails the suite.
- **What they hold.** Neither listing has a comment or a `schema` key. Listing 12.1's `controller`
  block carries a BACnet subnet, an IP address and a device id (`192.168.0.115/24`,
  `192.168.0.227`, `240001`): they are the specification's own sample values, from a private
  address range, and are kept because the fixture is verbatim. The repository's no-secret scan
  matches none of them.

The specification is published by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. The two listings are
quoted here as test inputs for a reader of the format they define.

## Where the two §12.7.3 files come from

- **Source:** the same chapter's §12.7.3 "Scenario 2: Control Input Obtained by Trending a Real
  Controller", on the same page: the `<pre>` block that follows "write the converted input time
  series to a new file reference_input.csv, using the format", and the one that follows "the file
  indicator.csv looks like".
- **Read on:** 2026-11-21, the same way as the listings: fetched with `curl`, the markup removed
  and the entities unescaped, nothing else changed. Each ends with the one line feed its block
  ends with: `obc_reference_input.csv` is 300 bytes and `obc_indicator.csv` 33.
- **What they hold.** Spaces around every value and header after the first, as the
  specification prints them; `tests/commissioning/trend_padded_files.rs` reads both as they are
  and pins their length and their first bytes.

## The canonical goldens are not blessed

`tests/commissioning/canonical_form.rs` compares `CommissioningSpec::to_canonical_json` and
`PointMapping::to_canonical_json` with the files under `canonical/` byte for byte, and
`CommissioningSpec::spec_id` with literals in the test. Neither was produced by this crate, and no
switch rewrites them: a golden made by the code it checks cannot fail.

[`derive_canonical.py`](derive_canonical.py) derives them. It is a second implementation of
comment removal, of the canonical form and of FNV-1a-128, in Python, sharing no code with the
crate:

- it removes `//` and `/* */` comments outside strings with one regular expression that reads a
  whole string, a whole line comment or a whole block comment at a time (the crate uses a
  byte-at-a-time state machine);
- it reads the rest with `json.loads`, keeping an integer token and a real apart (`parse_int`,
  `parse_float`);
- it gives a spec its `schema` tag when it has none;
- it writes every object's keys sorted by `key.encode("utf-8")`, at every depth, the `outputs`
  and `indicators` maps included: the order of a file's keys is no part of a spec;
- strings, integers, reals and the layout are written as
  [`../derive_canonical.py`](../derive_canonical.py) writes a vector set's, and the bytes are
  hashed with FNV-1a-128 over Python integers.

No test runs it. When the format changes in place, run it by hand from this directory for each
golden, review the diff, update the id literals in `tests/commissioning/canonical_form.rs`, and
say in the pull request which bytes moved and why:

```bash
for name in listing_12_1 listing_12_1_commented building_33 every_field listing_12_2; do
  python3 -I derive_canonical.py "$name.json" "canonical/$name.json"
done
```

It prints the id of each file's canonical bytes. For the four specs that is the `spec_id`; a
mapping file has no id of its own in the format, and the line it prints for `listing_12_2` is the
hash the test pins for that golden.
